nodes.label: Dual JSON parser strategy (JsonUtility default + optional Newtonsoft)
nodes.summary: glTFast maintains two parallel Schema/ implementations: a default Unity JsonUtility-based one and a Newtonsoft.Json-based one (compiled only when NEWTONSOFT_JSON is defined). Newtonsoft offers richer features (JsonExtensionData, polymorphic deserialization, full extras/extensions handling) but adds a dependency. JsonUtility is built-in and has no extra cost, but is limited. Keeping both lets users opt into Newtonsoft for fidelity without burdening users who only need basic glTF parsing. Schema POCOs map 1:1 to their non-Newtonsoft counterparts and inherit common base classes (e.g., AccessorBase) so downstream code can stay generic.

nodes.label: FakeSchema pre-pass parsing
nodes.summary: FakeSchema is a third, stripped-down schema variant used for fast pre-pass JSON deserialization. By declaring extension fields as plain strings (not nested types), it allows JsonUtility to detect which glTF extensions a file uses (or which sparse accessors exist) without paying the cost of full schema parsing. This lets the importer decide whether to load expensive code paths (Draco, Basis Universal, sparse accessor handling) before doing the heavy parse with the full Schema/. The GLTFAST_SAFE conditional gates sparse-accessor checks for a safer parsing mode.

nodes.label: Triple schema architecture
nodes.summary: glTFast maintains THREE parallel schema layers: (1) Schema/ for Unity JsonUtility full parse, (2) Newtonsoft/Schema/ for Newtonsoft.Json users, and (3) Schema/FakeSchema/ for cheap pre-pass extension/feature detection. This trades source-code duplication for runtime flexibility (JsonUtility being fast and AOT-safe, Newtonsoft being more capable, FakeSchema enabling early conditional code-path selection).
